newsitem.title: UK: British group concerned over banana workers' rights.
newsitem.headline: British group concerned over banana workers' rights.

text.p: A British watchdog group Sunday accused big banana companies of denying workers' rights in Costa Rica and urged consumers to complain by letter.

The World Development Movement, one of Britain's leading watchdog groups lobbying on behalf of the Third World, said multinational companies used potentially dangerous chemicals and banned trade unions on their plantations in Costa Rica.
The London-based group said it was not calling for a boycott by consumers but was urging poeple to write to the companies.

It said in a report that the expansion of banana production in Costa Rica meant that the Central American nation "uses eight times more pesticide per person than the world average; has one of the world's highest rates of pesticide poisoning and saw imports of pesticides shoot up by almost 50 percent between 1990 and 1994."
Harriet Lamb, an official at the group, compiled the report after visiting banana plantations in Costa Rica in June.

"Powerful banana companies are denying their employees basic human rights -- like the right to safe working conditions and to join a trade union. Workers told me that even mentioning the word union is dangerous," said Lamb.
Lamb said the group did not back a boycott but wanted consumers to lobby the firms for change on their plantations.
"We're not calling on people to stop buying bananas, just to write to the companies and call on them to clean up their act," said Lamb.
Dickon Poole, marketing manager of the British arm of Del Monte, one of the world's major fruit producers, said the company did not agree with the allegations but was investigating them.
"We have a very good brand name and are very concerned," he said. "But I do disagree."
